title: Verifiable product candidate artifacts
description: Faithful product artifacts and attributable metadata exchanged between production, release qualification, and verified installation, with candidate checks and published trust kept distinct.

operations.name: provide_product_candidate
operations.purpose: Supply an identified product candidate with its complete inventory and integrity basis.
inputs: Selected canonical source identity, declared supported target/product population, version/profile, and authorized transformations.
Actual production and validation observations, with unperformed or failed checks explicit.
outputs: Identified artifact set and member inventory, declared transformation/source identities, exact integrity metadata and algorithm/version domain, and actual validation scope/results.

For a browser-enabled candidate: exact profile/renderer/reading inventory, declared configuration matrix and independent customer/offline qualification; reference-site content has a separate identity.
behavior: Preserve canonical behavior and untransformed resources across the selected candidate; declare transformations and reject incomplete or unsupported content.
Generate outside canonical sources and active installation roots; production does not perform installation or customer state adoption.
Keep artifact bytes, file inventory, hash algorithm, counts, target/release identity, and metadata mutually consistent.

Provide only actual validation observations. The release consumer qualifies the exact retained candidate, and the installer establishes trust using its package-bundled metadata/release-index contract before accepting supplied bytes.

failure_behavior.condition: Inventory, transformation, dependency, metadata, or actual validation is missing, inconsistent, unsupported, or failed.
failure_behavior.outcome: Expose the affected candidate and block reliance on it as qualified or verified; do not synthesize passing metadata.

failure_behavior.condition: The selected artifact or algorithm is incompatible with its consumer.
failure_behavior.outcome: Reject incompatible consumption and retain the original identity; do not silently fall back or rewrite historical artifacts.

consistency_rules: Candidate production, qualified release, public availability, and verified installation are separate states; this artifact boundary cannot substitute one for another.
An installer must not trust an arbitrary local archive merely because it has a plausible filename or accompanying caller-provided metadata.
Retained artifact identities remain immutable across release authorization, public observation, and recovery; no false latest-version or publication claim follows from local production.

A browser-enabled CLI candidate must contain its declared runtime inputs and renderer resources without customer-side product generation or hidden acquisition. Existing skill archive trust and installation behavior remain unchanged.
compatibility_rules: Packaging, Installation, and Release retain their exact current targets, archive layouts, algorithms, bundled metadata/release-index trust rules, and independently versioned compatibility domains.
A new hash/metadata contract requires coordinated producer and consumer qualification; earlier published identities and supported historical verifier meanings are preserved.
The Interface is an artifact contract and does not prescribe a live package service or new acquisition endpoint.

sources.basis: Connect package production to release and installation using SRC-PUBLISHED-PACKAGING, SRC-PUBLISHED-INSTALLATION, and SRC-PUBLISHED-RELEASE; retain separate qualification, trust, and authority boundaries.

System and Architecture Design from SR-084–088 and refined SR-060; proposed responsibility, contract and realization only. No implementation, platform qualification or product availability is established.
